mainTopic: Items that are counted (דבר שיש בו מנין) are not nullified by a majority. A ברייתא about a ליטרא of untithed dried figs pressed onto an unknown container is brought as the source.
overview: The גמרא states a rule: an item that people count one by one (דבר שיש בו מנין) is too important to be nullified, even for a rabbinic prohibition, and all the more so for a Torah prohibition like the animals in the משנה. As a source, it quotes a ברייתא about a ליטרא of untithed dried figs that was pressed onto the top of one of many containers, and no one knows which one. In רבי מאיר's version, רבי אליעזר says the lower figs nullify the upper ones. In that version רבי יהושע says it takes a hundred openings, and otherwise the tops are forbidden and the bottoms permitted. In רבי יהודה's version, רבי אליעזר holds the hundred-openings view, and רבי יהושע says even three hundred openings do not help. Everyone agrees that figs lost somewhere inside one circle are nullified. רב אשי adds that even the רבנן agree living creatures are significant and are never nullified. The גמרא then asks why we can't pull out one animal at a time and rely on כל דפריש מרובא פריש. It answers that pulling an animal out ourselves makes it קבוע, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Counted items are never nullified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that a דבר שיש בו מנין is not בטל, even for a rabbinic prohibition, and all the more so for a Torah prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any item that is counted is not nullified, even when the prohibition is rabbinic. All the more so when it is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a general rule: something important enough that people count it does not get cancelled out by a majority. This applies even to rabbinic prohibitions, and certainly to Torah ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a small forbidden item mixed into a large permitted mixture becomes בטל. Here the גמרא says that when the item is the kind people count one by one, it is too important to disappear. The rule is built as a קל וחומר: if even a light rabbinic prohibition is not nullified, a Torah prohibition surely is not.

keyTerms.meaning: An item that is counted (sold or valued by the unit)
Becomes nullified, cancelled out in a mixture
A law from the Rabbis
A law from the Torah
All the more so (a קל וחומר)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains why some mixtures stay forbidden even when the forbidden part is tiny. It shows that the importance of an item can override the normal rule of majority.

phrases.english: Any item that has a count,
phrases.notes: He means things people count one by one because each unit is valuable.

phrases.english: even in a rabbinic law, is not nullified,
and all the more so in a Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of why the animals in the משנה are not nullified by stating the governing principle (the Torah-law case is the משנה's animals). The next step supports it with a source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A counted item is not בטל, whether the prohibition is דרבנן or, all the more so, דאוריתא.

steps.title: The case of the pressed dried figs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted about a ליטרא of untithed dried figs pressed onto one of several circles, barrels, or receptacles, where the person does not know which one.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: A ליטרא of dried figs was pressed onto the top of a fig circle, and he does not know which circle he pressed it onto. Or onto the top of a barrel, and he does not know which barrel. Or onto the top of a receptacle, and he does not know which receptacle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a source for the rule in Step 1. This step only sets up the case; the rulings come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A forbidden ליטרא of untithed figs became pressed onto the top of one container among many permitted ones, and we don't know which container. The ברייתא gives three versions of this case: fig circles, barrels, and straw receptacles. The question is whether the forbidden figs become בטל among all the permitted ones.

keyTerms.meaning: A ליטרא, a unit of weight
Dried figs
A circle (round cake) of pressed figs
A barrel
A straw receptacle (literally a beehive shape)

steps.confusionAlert: The forbidden figs did not get mixed all through the containers. They were pressed only onto the TOP of one container. That is why the next steps talk about the upper layers versus the lower ones.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
A ליטרא of dried figs,
phrases.notes: These figs are untithed, so they are forbidden until tithed.

phrases.english: that he pressed onto the top of a fig circle,
and he does not know onto which circle he pressed it;
onto the top of a barrel,
and he does not know onto which barrel he pressed it;
onto the top of a receptacle,
and he does not know onto which receptacle he pressed it —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the rule just stated.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a דבר שיש בו מנין is not בטל, even מדרבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a ליטרא of untithed dried figs pressed onto an unknown container.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the lower figs nullify the upper
steps.stepSummary: In רבי מאיר's version, רבי אליעזר treats the upper layers as loose pieces, so the permitted lower layers nullify them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says that רבי אליעזר says: We view the upper layers as if they were separate pieces, and the lower ones nullify the upper ones.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first opinion in the ברייתא, as רבי מאיר reports it. רבי אליעזר rules leniently: the forbidden figs on top become בטל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר does not treat the forbidden top layer as one important unit. He views it as loose pieces, so it mixes with all the permitted figs underneath. Since the permitted figs below far outnumber it, they nullify it.

keyTerms.meaning: We view, we treat as if
The upper layers
Separate, loose pieces
The lower layers
Nullify (literally 'raise up')

phrases.english: רבי מאיר says,
רבי אליעזר says:
We view the upper layers
as if they are separate pieces,
and the lower ones nullify the upper ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first ruling on the case set up in Step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The upper layers are viewed as separate pieces and are nullified by the lower layers, so no fig needs tithing.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: nullification needs a hundred openings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע holds that the forbidden figs are nullified only if there are a hundred container openings. Otherwise all the tops are forbidden and the bottoms are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: If there are a hundred openings, the forbidden figs are nullified. If not, the openings are forbidden and the bottoms are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second opinion in רבי מאיר's version, and it is stricter. רבי יהושע counts only the tops of the containers, not the figs underneath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהושע, the lower figs do not help nullify, because the forbidden ליטרא sits only on a top. So it must be nullified among the other tops, which requires a hundred of them. If there are fewer, every top layer is forbidden because any one could be the forbidden one, while the bottoms stay permitted because the forbidden figs never reached there.

keyTerms.meaning: Openings, the tops of the containers
They are nullified
If not
The bottoms, the lower parts of the containers

steps.whatToRemember: In רבי מאיר's version: רבי אליעזר says the lower figs join in and nullify the top. רבי יהושע says only the tops count, so nullification needs a hundred openings; otherwise the tops are forbidden and the bottoms are permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: The two opinions disagree about which figs count toward nullifying the forbidden ליטרא. The גמרא uses this ברייתא as its source for the rule about counted items.

phrases.english: רבי יהושע says:
If there are a hundred openings, they are nullified,
and if not,
the openings are forbidden
and the bottoms are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing, stricter view to רבי אליעזר's ruling in Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a hundred openings the forbidden figs are nullified. With fewer, all tops are forbidden and all bottoms are permitted.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's version: רבי אליעזר needs a hundred openings
steps.stepSummary: In רבי יהודה's version, רבי אליעזר holds the forbidden figs are nullified only if there are a hundred container openings. Otherwise all the tops are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says that רבי אליעזר says: If there are a hundred openings there, the forbidden figs are nullified. If not, all the openings (top layers) are forbidden, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives a second version of the argument, told by רבי יהודה. In his version, the opinion that needs a hundred openings belongs to רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי מאיר's version (Step 4), it was רבי יהושע who needed a hundred openings. רבי יהודה moves that opinion to רבי אליעזר. This frees up a stricter position for רבי יהושע in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Openings, meaning the top layers of the containers
Literally 'they go up'; here it means the forbidden part is nullified
Etc.; the rest of the quote is understood

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In רבי מאיר's version רבי יהושע needs a hundred openings. In רבי יהודה's version that same view belongs to רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says,
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ שָׁם מֵאָה פּוּמִּין – יַעֲלוּ,
phrases.english: If there are a hundred openings there, they are nullified,
and if not, the openings are forbidden, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." points back to the rest of the rule from Step 4: the bottom layers stay permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's version of the same argument, giving the hundred-openings view to רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, רבי אליעזר holds the pressed figs are nullified with a hundred openings. Otherwise the tops are forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: never nullified, even with three hundred openings
steps.stepSummary: In רבי יהודה's version, רבי יהושע holds the pressed figs are never nullified, even among three hundred openings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: Even if there are three hundred openings there, they are not nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside רבי יהודה's version, רבי יהושע gives the strictest view: no number of openings is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'even three hundred' shows that the number doesn't matter at all. For רבי יהושע, this kind of item is significant and is never nullified, even though it is not always sold by count. This is the strictest view so far.

keyTerms.meaning: Three hundred; a big number to show that no amount helps
They are not nullified

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ שָׁם שְׁלֹשָׁה מֵאוֹת פּוּמִּין –
phrases.english: Even if there are three hundred openings there,
they are not nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ שָׁם שְׁלֹשָׁה מֵאוֹת פּוּמִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion within רבי יהודה's version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, רבי יהושע holds that this item is never nullified, no matter how many openings there are.

steps.title: Everyone agrees when the spot inside one circle is unknown
steps.stepSummary: If the figs were pressed into one circle but no one knows where in it, everyone agrees they are nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he pressed it into a circle of figs and does not know where in the circle he pressed it, whether on its north side or its south side, everyone agrees it is nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה ends with a case where there is no argument at all: the forbidden figs got mixed into one circle at an unknown spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier cases, the forbidden figs sit as a whole layer on top of one specific container. Here they are lost somewhere inside a single circle and can't be picked out. So even רבי יהושע doesn't treat them as a significant item, and they are nullified.

keyTerms.meaning: He pressed it (the ליטרא of figs)
A circle (a round cake) of pressed dried figs
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: In רבי יהודה's version: רבי אליעזר says the figs are nullified with a hundred openings. רבי יהושע says they are never nullified. But if the figs are lost at an unknown spot inside one circle, everyone agrees they are nullified.

phrases.english: If he pressed it into a circle,
and does not know
in which place in the circle he pressed it,
whether to its north or to its south,
everyone agrees it is nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרָסָהּ בְּעִיגּוּל, וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ בְּאֵיזֶה מְקוֹם בְּעִיגּוּל דְּרָסָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the argument by giving a case where both sides agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Figs pressed at an unknown spot inside one circle are nullified according to everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא shows where the משנה's ruling comes from. The משנה says animals in the mixture are not nullified, and that fits רבי יהושע in רבי יהודה's version, who holds that even an item only sometimes sold by count is never nullified. In the next step רב אשי offers a different way to explain the משנה.

steps.title: רב אשי: living creatures are significant and are never nullified
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the משנה can follow even the רבנן, because living animals are significant and are not nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: You can even say the משנה follows the רבנן, because living creatures are significant and are not nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a different way to explain why the משנה says animals are not nullified. He does not need to tie it to רבי יהושע's strict view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the ברייתא, one could say the משנה follows רבי יהושע in רבי יהודה's version, who says items are never nullified. רב אשי says that isn't needed. Even the רבנן (רבי מאיר's version), who usually let such items be nullified, agree that live animals are special. They are significant in themselves and are never nullified.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say
The Rabbis; here, the side that usually allows nullification
Living creatures
They are significant (important)
They are nullified

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a separate reason why living animals are never nullified: they are important in themselves. So the rule about animals does not depend on the general argument about counted items.
steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to explain the משנה: (1) it follows רבי יהושע in רבי יהודה's version, who says such items are never nullified; (2) רב אשי says even the רבנן agree, because living creatures are always significant.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
You can even say it follows the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה about animals that are not nullified can fit even the more lenient side.

phrases.english: living creatures are significant
and are not nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the משנה that does not depend on רבי יהושע's strict view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason: living creatures are significant in themselves.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה had to follow the strict view that such items are never nullified (רבי יהושע in רבי יהודה's version).
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the lenient רבנן agree that living animals are never nullified, because they are significant.

steps.title: Why not take out one animal at a time from the majority?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we can't pull out one animal at a time and offer it, relying on the rule that whatever separates comes from the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us pull out one of the animals and offer it, and say: anything that separates, separates from the majority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that all the animals in the mixture are forbidden. It suggests a way to use them anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the animals are not nullified, as רב אשי said in Step 8, there is another tool: כל דפריש מרובא פריש. Most of the animals are fit, so any single animal we pull out should be treated as one of the fit ones. That would let us offer them one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us draw out / pull out
Let us offer (on the מזבח)
Whatever separates from a group is treated as coming from the majority

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same as ביטול (nullification). Step 8 said living animals are never nullified. Here the גמרא uses a different rule: each animal pulled out is judged by the majority.

phrases.english: And let us pull out and offer one of them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the mixed-up animals in the משנה: a few unfit animals among many fit offerings.

phrases.english: and say: whatever separates, separates from the majority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that living animals are not nullified (Step 8), but proposes a different way to permit them: separating one at a time.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that all the animals in the mixture are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even without ביטול, the rule of כל דפריש מרובא פריש should let each animal pulled out count as fit, because most of the mixture is fit.

steps.title: Pulling an animal out of its place makes it fixed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that pulling an animal out of the group counts as taking it from its fixed place, so it is קבוע and the majority rule does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we pull one out?! That would make it fixed (קבוע).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Pulling the animal out yourself means it is taken from its fixed place, so it counts as קבוע. The sentence keeps going right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of כל דפריש only works when an item leaves the group on its own, away from where it was fixed. When we reach into the mixture and take one from where it stands, it is still treated as being in its fixed place. In that case the majority does not decide.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixed: an item still in its set place, where the majority rule does not apply
It becomes / it is considered

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think קבוע means the animal is tied down. It is a legal status: being taken straight from its place in the mixture, so the majority cannot decide for it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between פריש (separated on its own) and קבוע (taken from its fixed place) is a basic tool used all over ש"ס for doubts in mixtures.

phrases.english: Should we pull one out?! It would be considered fixed,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge of Step 9 by showing the majority rule does not apply here.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of a rule: כל דפריש does not apply to an item taken from its fixed place.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any animal pulled out of the mixture is judged by the majority and is fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pulling it out ourselves makes it קבוע, so the majority rule cannot permit it, and the משנה's ruling stands.
